kit.title: Articulatory vocal tract: stress, release, nasals, lax vowels

clips.title: isolated /ɪ/ 180 ms, 140 Hz. Measured: Burg F1/F2 375/2024 Hz; tube chain 346/1987 (+8.5/+1.8 %); Hillenbrand 1995 male 429/2034 (-12.5/-0.5 %); Peterson & Barney 392/1993 (-4.3/+1.5 %). Present in the DSL table and renderable. PREDICTION: heard as the vowel of 'bit' (or a slightly high, 'ee'-leaning version of it). FALSIFIED if heard as 'ee' of 'beet', as 'eh' of 'bet', or as a different phone.
clips.reason: It's more like the eu in cordon bleu than the i in bit

clips.title: ba with the plosive burst (gain 0.06, a design value). Measured: burst alone peaks 0.0142 at 85 ms = -24.0 dB re vowel peak, falls to a tenth in 17 ms, burst rms in the 30 ms after its peak -31.0 dB re vowel rms. PREDICTION: a slightly crisper, more 'b'-like onset than B/off; the burst is quiet and short so the difference is small, 'a little pop' at most. FALSIFIED if it sounds like a hiss, a click, or a separate noise after the vowel started, or if no difference is heard.
clips.feel: the syllable 'bah' with a clean, crisp 'b' at the start
clips.reason: More like fah then bah but you can hear something there

clips.title: ba with the release_flow splines dropped (WordRender --no-burst). Measured: closure peak 0.0078 (voice bar), release (voicing breaking through)peak 0.1087 = -6.3 dB re vowel peak 0.2247, no burst noise. PREDICTION: a soft, voiced 'b' with the vowel starting smoothly; may sound slightly 'w'-like or lack the pop. FALSIFIED if listeners cannot hear any difference from the burst twin (then burst gain 0.06 is inaudible).
clips.feel: the syllable 'bah' with a soft start
clips.reason: There is no audible constriction. While the vowel is recognizable, it still sounds like a kazoo

clips.title: nibu, no stress marks. Measured: /i/ 150-250 ms rms vs the stressed render +0.21 dB; unstressed vowel 180 ms, f0 139.9 Hz. PREDICTION: reads asan even two-syllable word with no strong first syllable. FALSIFIED if listeners hear it as stressed on a syllable or cannot tell it from the stressed twin.
clips.feel: a made-up two-syllable word, 'nee-boo', both syllables even
clips.reason: These both sound like 'ee'oo, with both consonants you're going for being just clicks

clips.title: nibu with primary stress on /i/ (NI-bu). Measured: /i/ 247 ms vs 180 ms (+75 ms; design +68), f0 148.1 vs 139.9 Hz (x1.059), amplitude factor 1.30; level of /i/ in the 150-250 ms window only +0.21 dB (five-vowel mean +1.93 dB, per vowel +1.2 to +3.0). PREDICTION: first syllable heard as the prominent one, mostly through length and pitch, little through loudness; B should be picked as 'stressed on the first syllable'. FALSIFIED if it sounds no more prominent than the flat twin, if it sounds like a question or a pitch accent rather than stress, or if the level is what is heard (then the f0-scatter question is wrong).
clips.feel: the same made-up word, with the first syllable stronger: 'NEE-boo'

clips.title: isolated /i/ 180 ms at 140 Hz, no stress. Measured: level 100-170 ms is the reference. PREDICTION: plain short vowel. FALSIFIED if it already sounds emphasised.
clips.reason: Still spoken by a kazoo with a two pack a day smoking habit, but it's an ee

clips.title: isolated /i/ with primary stress: 247 ms, f0 x1.06, amplitude 1.30. Measured against the flat /i/: +1.22 dB total (f0 rise alone -0.80 dB, the amplitude and the rest +2.02 dB). PREDICTION: heard as longer and a little higher; the 1.2 dB louder is under what a listener can judge, so 'longer and higher' is the answer, 'louder' is not. FALSIFIED if it sounds the same length and pitch, or clearly louder.
clips.feel: the same 'ee' vowel, held longer and said with emphasis

clips.title: isolated /ʊ/ 180 ms, 140 Hz. Measured: Burg F1/F2 486/894 Hz; tube chain 478/850 (+1.7/+5.2 %); Hillenbrand 469/1123 (+3.7/-20.4 %); Peterson &Barney 437/1023 (+11.3/-12.6 %). Present in the DSL table and renderable. PREDICTION: heard as the vowel of 'book', probably darker or rounder than a natural one (F2 20 % under the population mean, the back-vowel gap). FALSIFIED if heard as 'oo' of 'boot', 'o' of 'boat' or 'uh' of 'but'.
clips.reason: It's distinguishable, but it strongly has that reedy quality which I associate with pink trombone and that new one I shared

clips.title: nibu (flat) after the fix: release_flow is zero outside its own plosive. Same audio as stress-nibu-flat, kept as its own clip so the before/after pair is one-to-one. Measured: leak 0.0 from 275 ms on, burst of the b itself unchanged (bin 0.0226 at 81 ms before and after). PREDICTION: clean hum into thevowel, no noisy onset; preferred over 'before' if the leak is audible. FALSIFIED if 'before' is preferred or no difference is heard.
clips.feel: a made-up word that should start with a clean, smooth hum into the vowel: 'nee-boo'
clips.reason: Just slightly less reverse attack on this one

clips.title: nibu (flat) rendered at main c0e6b98, before the release_flow fix. Measured: burst-gain leak vs the fixed render, peak 0.0688 and rms 0.0067 inthe leading /n/ (0-95 ms; the /n/ itself is rms 0.0058, so the hiss is louder than the murmur), peak 0.0504 over /i/ onset 95-150 ms, 0.0019 after; whole-render peak 0.487 vs 0.399. PREDICTION: an audible hiss or click as the /n/ opens into the vowel, the first sound of the word being a noisy 'sn'-like or 'tsh' onset instead of a clean nasal hum. FALSIFIED if the two are indistinguishable (then the leak is inaudible and the fix is cosmetic).
clips.feel: a made-up word that should start with a clean, smooth hum into the vowel: 'nee-boo'
clips.reason: 'Ee'oo with some odd clicks that sound more like a reversed percussive hit than a consonant

clips.title: /ɑnɑ/. Measured: murmur -9.64 dB re the flanking vowels (2.17 dB above /m/; the gap is 2.01/2.17/2.05/1.61 dB at f0 110/140/170/200 Hz, so not harmonic sampling), Burg N1 332 Hz, bands 38.4/28.2/16.8/0.9 dB. PREDICTION: heard as 'ah-nah', a tongue-tip hum, a shade stronger than the /m/ one; the 2 dB isnot expected to be noticed. FALSIFIED if heard as 'ama' or 'anga', if it sounds much louder than the /m/ clip, or if there is hiss.
clips.feel: 'ah-nah': the tongue touches behind the teeth for a soft hum between two open vowels
clips.reason: It just sounds like a basket ball buzzer, no audible articulation

clips.title: bun, /bʊn/, no burst. Measured: closure peak 0.0043, release peak 0.1074 = -5.9 dB re vowel peak 0.2126. PREDICTION: soft 'b' then a short backvowel then a nasal; the final /n/ is a clean hum (no leak since the fix). FALSIFIED as for burst-ba-off.
clips.feel: a short word like 'bunn' or 'boon' said quickly, soft start
clips.reason: Oou'mou is what this sounds closest to, with the apostrophe representing a clicking sound that's in there

clips.title: bun, /bʊn/, with burst. Measured: burst peak 0.0130 at 81 ms = -24.3 dB re vowel peak, tenth in 15 ms; tail leak after the fix 0.0 (was 0.0126 at the end before). PREDICTION: slightly crisper onset than off; final /n/ clean. FALSIFIED as for burst-ba-on.
clips.feel: a short word like 'bunn' or 'boon' said quickly, crisp 'b' start
clips.reason: The main difference seems to be a sort of air release added to the beginning which resembles more a truck releasing its pneumatics than a human

clips.title: /ɑmɑ/. Measured: murmur -11.81 dB re the flanking vowels (design band -16..-8), Burg N1 295 Hz, band levels 0-400/400-800/800-1600/1600-3200 Hzof the murmur 36.3/23.6/21.3/2.7 dB. PREDICTION: heard as 'ah-mah', a lip-closed hum between the vowels, clearly softer than the vowels. FALSIFIED if heard as 'abah' or 'awah', if the hum is as loud as the vowels, or if there is a gap or click.
clips.feel: 'ah-mah': lips close for a soft hum between two open vowels
clips.reason: That m is almost coming through, still more of a basketball buzzer
